This site hosts four independent, self-contained textbooks written from algebraic and combinatorial definitions for competitive programmers who already have a tested algorithm library. Use the top navigation bar or the links below to switch between textbooks; each book maintains its own sidebar navigation, study plan, notation reference, and problem archive.

---

## Textbook I · Formal Power Series & Generating Functions (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`)

**[Enter the Formal Power Series Textbook →](fps/index.qmd)** · [Study Plan (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`)](fps/study-plan.qmd) · [Notation & 16 Failure Modes](fps/notation.qmd) · [321-Problem Archive](fps/capstones/problem-archive-guide.qmd) · [Bibliography & Rosetta Stone](fps/sources.qmd) · [Download Offline HTML (`.zip`)](downloads/icpc-fps-offline.zip)

A rigorous, zero-forward-reference **6-Part, 24-Chapter** monograph on Formal Power Series ($K[[x]]$, $K((x))$) and Generating Functions for ICPC, Codeforces, AtCoder, and Universal Cup contests:

- **Scope:** Valuation topology $\nu(F)$ and 1D/coupled Newton iteration (`inv`, `sqrt`, `ln`, `exp`, `pow`), $O(NK)$ sparse differential recurrences, the unlabeled ($\operatorname{SEQ}, \operatorname{MSET}, \operatorname{PSET}$) and labeled ($\operatorname{SET}, \operatorname{CYC}$, Boxed Product) Symbolic Method, Bostan–Mori and Berlekamp–Massey, Snake Oil and Stirling/Taylor shifts, roots-of-unity filters and cyclotomic rings, run-length and Goulden–Jackson cluster sieves, online CDQ/relaxed convolutions, formal Laurent residues and 6-form Lagrange Inversion, cactus/block-cut/DAG/SCC graphical series, stochastic PGFs, 1D/2D kernel methods, the 5-ring bivariate hierarchy and Furstenberg diagonals, D-finite ODEs and $p$-adic indicial lifting, Tellegen transposition (`mulT`, multipoint `eval`/`interp`), Kinoshita–Li $O(N \log^2 N)$ `power_projection`/`compose`/`revert`, Static Top Tree DP, $q$-analogues, Set Power Series $\mathcal{R}_n$, and Dirichlet series $\mathcal{D}_f$.
- **Practice & Assessment:** **192** inline chapter ladder problems (`2 Stepping Stones`, `2 Intermediate`, `2 Advanced`, `2 Mastery` per chapter), **6** Two-Stage Blind Topic-Group Checkpoints ([`CP-I`](fps/checkpoints/cp01-part1-foundations.qmd)–[`CP-VI`](fps/checkpoints/cp06-part6-trees-qseries-sps-dirichlet.qmd), 48 problems), and a **14-problem** [Multi-Perspective Synthesis Reserve](fps/capstones/synthesis-reserve.qmd) (`Syn-01`–`Syn-14`).
- **Start here:** [FPS Overview](fps/index.qmd) or directly at [Ch 01 · The Ring $K[[x]]$, Valuation Topology & Newton Inversion](fps/chapters/ch01-ring-convolutions-newton-inv.qmd).

## Textbook II · Network Flows, Minimum Cuts, Matching, Duality & Modelling (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`)

**[Enter the Network Flows & Modelling Textbook →](flows/index.qmd)** · [Study Plan & 3-Axis Diagnostic](flows/study-plan.qmd) · [Notation & 24 Failure Modes](flows/notation.qmd) · [320-Problem Archive](flows/capstones/problem-archive-guide.qmd) · [Bibliography & Rosetta Stone](flows/sources.qmd) · [Download Offline HTML (`.zip`)](downloads/icpc-flows-offline.zip)

A rigorous, zero-forward-reference **6-Part, 24-Chapter** modelling-first monograph dedicated to recognizing hidden flow, minimum-cut, matching, and LP-dual structures in problem statements with **no graphs mentioned at all** (`Direction A: Non-Graph -> Flow`) and eliminating flow solvers into $O(N \log N)$ algorithms when $N \le 2 \times 10^5$ (`Direction B: Flow -> Fast Algorithm`):

- **Scope:** Flow-cut duality, Picard–Queyranne residual condensation DAGs, feasible vs. essential cut edges (`[AHOI2009]`), incremental flow rollback (`退流`, `[SDOI2014] LIS`), vertex/time splitting, lower-bound circulations (`上下界网络流`) and Hoffman's theorem, König–Hall–Dilworth duality, Dulmage–Mendelsohn (`DM`) decomposition and bipartite walk games, Birkhoff–von Neumann and regular edge coloring (`AGC 037 D`), segment-tree Hall Marriage elimination (`ARC 076 F`), Maximum Weight Closure (`最大权闭合子图`), submodular pseudo-Boolean cut compilation (`燃やす埋める`), Bipartite Variable Inversion (`二部グラフの片側反転`, `AGC 038 F — Two Permutations`), multi-state unary threshold chains and disjunctive OR cuts (`ARC 107 F — Sum of Abs`, `ARC 142 E — Pairing Wizards`), Ishikawa convex Monge penalties, the Discrete Coarea Formula (`CF 1427 G — One Billion Shades of Grey`), 0-1 fractional programming (`Dinkelbach`), Maximum Density Subgraphs, planar $s$-$t$ and $k$-terminal dual shortest paths (`[NOI2010] 海拔`, `[CSP-S 2021] 交通规划`), min-cut DP (`CF 724 E`, `CF 1919 F2`), Gomory–Hu cut trees, MCMF Johnson potentials, negative-cycle saturation, convex marginal edge splitting, Consecutive Equation Differencing (`[NOI2008] 志愿者招募`), cycle covers, dynamic scheduling, coordinate-rank slots (`AGC 031 E`), Manhattan $2^d$ hubs (`AGC 034 D`), explicit LP duality, Totally Unimodular (TU) matrices, DS-accelerated flow graphs (`线段树/主席树优化建图`), Edmonds' Blossom and Tutte matrix, Simulated MCMF (`模拟费用流 / 反悔贪心`), and $L_p$ Isotonic Regression (`保序回归`).
- **Practice & Assessment:** **192** inline chapter ladder problems (`#001`–`#192`, each compiled via the **4-Step "Zero Magic Gadgets" Standard**), **6** Part-End Blind Recognition Checkpoints ([`CP-I`](flows/checkpoints/cp01-part1-foundations.qmd)–[`CP-VI`](flows/checkpoints/cp06-part6-ds-blossom-simulated-isotonic.qmd), `#193`–`#240`), and a **16-problem** [Grandmaster Synthesis Reserve](flows/capstones/synthesis-reserve.qmd) (`#241`–`#256`).
- **Start here:** [Network Flows Overview](flows/index.qmd) or directly at [Ch 01 · Conservation Laws, Residual Graphs, and Max-Flow Min-Cut Duality](flows/chapters/ch01-conservation-residual-maxflow-mincut.qmd).

## Textbook III · Competitive Programming Mathematics (`00`–`20`)

**[Enter the Competitive Programming Mathematics Textbook →](math/index.qmd)** · [Study Plan (`00`–`20`)](math/study-plan.qmd) · [Notation & Contracts](math/notation.qmd) · [Sources & Policy](math/sources.qmd) · [Download Offline HTML (`.zip`)](downloads/icpc-math-offline.zip)

A broad **21-Chapter** foundation and synthesis curriculum covering the general mathematical pillars of competitive programming from first principles:

- **Part I · Arithmetic and counting (`00`–`05`):** [Foundations and proof](math/00-foundations/chapter.qmd), [modular algebra](math/01-modular-algebra/chapter.qmd), [multiplicative number theory](math/02-multiplicative-number-theory/chapter.qmd), [combinatorics](math/03-combinatorics/chapter.qmd), [binomials modulo anything](math/04-modular-binomials/chapter.qmd), and [group actions (Burnside/Pólya)](math/05-group-actions/chapter.qmd).
- **Part II · Algebraic engines (`06`–`11`):** [Polynomials and FFT/NTT](math/06-polynomials/chapter.qmd), [linear algebra](math/07-linear-algebra/chapter.qmd), [subset and divisor transforms](math/08-transforms/chapter.qmd), [formal power series overview](math/09-formal-power-series/chapter.qmd), [generating functions overview](math/10-generating-functions/chapter.qmd), and [set power series](math/11-set-power-series/chapter.qmd).
- **Part III · Models and synthesis (`12`–`15`):** [Probability and Markov chains](math/12-probability/chapter.qmd), [discrete sums and floor geometry](math/13-discrete-sums/chapter.qmd), [summatory sieves](math/14-advanced-sieves/chapter.qmd), and [mixed capstones](math/15-capstones/chapter.qmd).
- **Part IV · Frontier topics (`16`–`20`):** [$q$-analogues and subspaces](math/16-q-analogues/chapter.qmd), [finite-field polynomials](math/17-finite-field-polynomials/chapter.qmd), [algebraic graph methods (Pfaffians/Tutte)](math/18-algebraic-graph-methods/chapter.qmd), [holonomic methods](math/19-holonomic-methods/chapter.qmd), and [frontier capstones](math/20-frontier-capstones/chapter.qmd).
- **Start here:** [Mathematics Overview](math/index.qmd) or directly at [00 · Mathematical foundations and proof](math/00-foundations/chapter.qmd).

## Textbook IV · Advanced Strings & Word Combinatorics (`Ch 01`–`Ch 30`)

**[Enter the Advanced Strings & Word Combinatorics Textbook →](strings/index.qmd)** · [Study Plan & Diagnostic Router (`Ch 01`–`Ch 30`)](strings/study-plan.qmd) · [Notation & Word Invariants](strings/notation.qmd) · [337-Problem Archive](strings/capstones/problem-archive-guide.qmd) · [Bibliography & Rosetta Stone](strings/sources.qmd) · [Download Offline HTML (`.zip`)](downloads/icpc-strings-offline.zip)

A rigorous, zero-forward-reference **7-Part, 30-Chapter** monograph on combinatorics on words, structural periodicity, suffix structures, palindromic and compressed pattern matching, string generating functions, and algebraic stringology:

- **Scope:** Period–border duality, the Fine–Wilf theorem and sub-threshold orbit counting (`Ch 01`), the Weak Periodicity Lemma and $O(\log N)$ border arithmetic progressions (`Ch 02`), border-group modulo shortest path (`同余最短路`, `[WC2016] 论战捆竹竿`, `Ch 03`), series-link (`slink`/`diff`) DP acceleration on KMP and PAM (`CF 932G`, `CF 906E`, `Ch 04`), Chen–Fox–Lyndon factorization, Duval's automaton, RLE Duval and necklace/BBWT bijections (`Ch 05`), Significant Suffixes (`显著后缀`, `[ZJOI2017] 字符串`, `[JSOI2019] 节日庆典`, `Ch 06`), Lyndon arrays and Min-Cartesian Lyndon trees (`Ch 07`), the Runs Theorem ($\rho(N) < N$) and 2D square sweeps (`[NOI2016] 优秀的拆分`, `Ch 08`), SAM/DAWG vs. Suffix Tree duality and Trie-BFS GSAM (`Ch 09`), `endpos` segment tree merging (`[NOI2018] 你的名字`, `Ch 10`), dynamic SAM with LCT and border stratification (`Ch 11`), `SA-IS` and $\text{rk}$-descent counting (`AGC 060 D`, `Ch 12`), Virtual Suffix Trees and $2N \log_2 N$ DSU-on-Tree dominant pairs (`Ch 13`), `CDAWG`, persistent SAM, `SCDAWG`, and Dietz–Sleator suffix balanced trees (`Ch 14`), 6-method internal pattern matching (`[BJWC2018] Border 的四种求法`, `Ch 15`), deterministic/tree/4-way deque PAM (`Ch 16`), $O(1)$ range LPS and rich words (`Ch 17`), 1-NTT wildcard & involution matching (`Ch 18`), $k$-mismatch wavefronts & $2k$-period dichotomy (`Ch 19`), parameterized/order/Cartesian KMP & weighted strings (`Ch 20`), Locally Consistent Parsing (Jeż recompression), SLPs, and String Attractors (`Ch 21`), `DASG`, Hébrard's arch factorization, Simon's congruence & invertible subsequence matrices (`Ch 22`), bit-parallel LCS and Tiskin's Seaweed (`海草矩阵`) Unit-Monge $\boxdot$ (`Ch 23`), Goulden–Jackson cluster GFs and $t=1+u$ moment shift (`Ch 24`), Conway martingale PGFs and `DP套DP` (`Ch 25`), word equations with signed/parallel DSU and $10^{18}$ period folding (`Ch 26`), inverse string reconstruction and SA inequality digraphs (`Ch 27`), De Bruijn BEST theorem, Wheeler graphs, and Nishimoto–Tabei $O(1)$ RLBWT Move structures (`Ch 28`), tree strings (`[CTSC2010] 珠宝商`), stack-trie path isomorphism, and non-abelian $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ hashing (`Ch 29`), and Sturmian, Rytter singular (`[周任飞 2017]`), Thue–Morse, and morphic words (`Ch 30`).
- **Practice & Assessment:** **255+** inline 4-tier chapter ladder problems (`Stepping Stone` $\to$ `Intermediate` $\to$ `Advanced` $\to$ `Mastery`), **7** Part-End Blind Checkpoints ([`CP-I`](strings/checkpoints/cp01-part1-periodicity-borders-slink.qmd)–[`CP-VII`](strings/checkpoints/cp07-part7-equations-trees-groups-morphic.qmd), 52 problems with Diagnostic Decoy Pairs), and a **30-problem** [Grandmaster Multi-Part Synthesis Reserve](strings/capstones/synthesis.qmd) (`Syn-01`–`Syn-30`).
- **Start here:** [Advanced Strings Overview](strings/index.qmd) or directly at [Ch 01 · Period–Border Duality, the Fine–Wilf Theorem, and Sub-Threshold Orbit Counting](strings/chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd).

## Which Textbook Should You Read?

| Your Goal | Recommended Entry Point | Offline HTML Bundle |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Master generating functions, polynomial operators, tree/graph enumeration, bivariate diagonals, ODEs, or Set Power Series in depth | **[Textbook I · Formal Power Series (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`)](fps/index.qmd)** | **[`icpc-fps-offline.zip`](downloads/icpc-fps-offline.zip)** |
| Recognize hidden flow/min-cut/matching/MCMF models in non-graph problems (`燃やす埋める`, `切糕`, LP duality, `模拟费用流`, `保序回归`) | **[Textbook II · Network Flows & Modelling (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`)](flows/index.qmd)** | **[`icpc-flows-offline.zip`](downloads/icpc-flows-offline.zip)** |
| Build general foundations in proof, modular arithmetic, number theory, linear algebra, probability, and sublinear sieves | **[Textbook III · Competitive Programming Mathematics (`00`–`20`)](math/index.qmd)** | **[`icpc-math-offline.zip`](downloads/icpc-math-offline.zip)** |
| Master combinatorics on words, border APs, Lyndon/Runs theory, SAM/PAM/Suffix Tree dominance, Seaweed matrices, and SLPs | **[Textbook IV · Advanced Strings & Word Combinatorics (`Ch 01`–`Ch 30`)](strings/index.qmd)** | **[`icpc-strings-offline.zip`](downloads/icpc-strings-offline.zip)** |
| Keep all four textbooks in one local archive | **[All Four Textbooks Combined](index.qmd)** | **[`icpc-all-books-offline.zip`](downloads/icpc-all-books-offline.zip)** |

Each offline `.zip` archive bundles the complete multi-page HTML textbook with local KaTeX math rendering (`assets/katex/`), sidebar navigation, light/dark mode, collapsible solution callouts, and `file://`-compatible offline full-text search—unzip and open `index.html` in any browser without an internet connection.
